title: AgentX 1.0 / InferenceX v3: does the CUDA moat hold up in agentic inferencing?
gist: An open benchmark that replays 393 anonymised coding-agent sessions: many turns, contexts up to a million tokens, heavy prefix reuse, bursts of sub-agents. Every data point is a public CI run with its configuration committed. It replaced fixed-length request benchmarks as the number serving teams compete on.
changes: This is the hill everyone is climbing. Almost every result tracked here is stated against it. A shared, replayable workload is what made agent-driven optimisation possible outside the companies that own traffic. It is also a single target the whole field can overfit.
caveats: One organisation's coding traces now define good serving. The post counts upstream fixes inconsistently (50+ and 70+) and many were still open. Part of the article is paywalled.

bears_on.note: Replaying real agent sessions instead of fixed-length requests changed which optimisations matter.
A public replayable workload lowers the traffic moat, and at the same time points everyone at one trace set.
Fifty or more fixes it prompted went upstream into vLLM and SGLang.
